what: Every eligible EdgeDesk pregame forecast, locked before the game and graded against the verified final, misses included. Research, not picks.

VERIFIED.label: Verified pregame
VERIFIED.means: Captured by the performance ledger from a public, committed EdgeDesk artifact before the game started, hash-chained and committed.

RECORDED.label: Recorded pregame (pre-ledger)
RECORDED.means: Imported from an earlier EdgeDesk pregame-only record. Its own timestamp is before the start, but the performance ledger did not lock it, so it is never counted in the verified headline.

coverage.label: MLB
coverage.why: no per-game MLB projection is published: the history engine (mlb/history) is walk-forward through 2025 with end-of-2025 ratings and no 2026 or postseason inputs, and the run model (mlb/engine.js) runs in the browser only and is unvalidated

coverage.label: College baseball

coverage.label: UFC / MMA
coverage.why: no fighter model is built: the 2024 Elo test does not beat a coin flip (engine/lab/ufc_elo.json: 138 scored bouts, log loss 0.689 vs 0.693, interval includes zero)

rules: A forecast is on the record only if it was captured or recorded before the game started. A later number is refused, never stored.
The graded forecast is the last one the ledger captured before the actual start. Every earlier revision is kept, and none is ever overwritten.

Verified pregame means the ledger itself captured the forecast from a public, committed EdgeDesk artifact before the start. Forecasts imported from EdgeDesk’s earlier records are labelled recorded pregame and never counted in the verified headline.
A final is verified when every source that has the game agrees on integer scores. Sources that disagree settle nothing. A corrected final is a new revision, and the old one is kept.
Canceled, forfeited and long-postponed games are void, never counted as wins or losses. A forecast made for a date that moved by more than 36 hours is not the forecast for the game that was played.
A rate, Brier score or average error is printed only once 20 games stand behind it. Smaller samples show their counts.
Market comparisons use only a named-book quote captured before the start. No price, no units. No legitimate close from the same source, no CLV. A fair-line gap is not a betting result.
